name: Lorcaserin (Belviq)
lead: Lorcaserin, sold as Belviq and Belviq XR, is a selective serotonin 5-HT2C receptor agonist that was prescribed for chronic weight management, developed by Arena Pharmaceuticals and approved by the US FDA on 27 June 2012. [1][2] It helped people look leaner by reducing appetite: through satiety signalling in the brain, patients ate less and lost body weight and, in trials that measured it, abdominal fat. [2][21]

In three placebo-controlled trials of nearly 8,000 participants it produced an average weight loss of roughly 3 to 3.7 percent more than placebo over up to a year, alongside diet and exercise counselling. [2] About 47 percent of people without diabetes lost at least 5 percent of body weight, versus about 23 percent on placebo. [2]

In February 2020 the FDA asked the manufacturer to withdraw it after a large safety trial found more cancer diagnoses among people taking it than on placebo, and approval was withdrawn in September 2020. [2] Lorcaserin is no longer marketed in the US. No appearance-community discussion of it was identified beyond a passing mention of Belviq in a forum thread among weight-loss drugs a family member was considering. [28]

paras: Lorcaserin was approved for adults with a body mass index of 30 or higher, or 27 or higher with a weight-related condition, as an adjunct to diet and exercise. [2] An extended-release once-daily version was approved in July 2016. [2] Labelling advised stopping the drug in patients who had not lost 5 percent of body weight after 12 weeks. [2] Obesity treatment guidelines and reviews published during this period described it among the available weight-loss medications. [3][4][5]

For people seeking a leaner physique, lorcaserin worked on the intake side of energy balance, rather than on exercise or metabolism. A randomised placebo-controlled 6-month trial reported abdominal fat loss with improvements in the circulating metabolome and lipidome, and no change in the myostatin-activin-follistatin-IGF-1 axes that regulate muscle growth. [21]

Three placebo-controlled trials (BLOOM, BLOSSOM and BLOOM-DM) tested lorcaserin in overweight or obese adults, with and without type 2 diabetes, lasting 52 to 104 weeks. [2][6][7][8] In people without diabetes, about 47 percent lost at least 5 percent of body weight versus about 23 percent on placebo; in people with type 2 diabetes the figures were 38 percent versus 16 percent. [2] A separate analysis examined glycaemic parameters in patients with type 2 diabetes. [22]

A JAMA systematic review and meta-analysis comparing obesity drugs, and an earlier JAMA review of long-term obesity drug treatment, placed its effect among the more modest in the class. [9][10] The authors of a 2018 New England Journal of Medicine editorial discussed the drug's benefits and safety questions together. [23] A randomised trial examined lorcaserin with lifestyle counselling for maintaining weight lost on a low-calorie diet, [24] and a small crossover study investigated biomarkers that predict who responds to the drug. [25]

Because the earlier weight-loss drug fenfluramine caused heart valve disease through serotonin 5-HT2B receptors, valve safety was a focus. A 2016 phase 3 trial found valvulopathy in 2.4 percent of lorcaserin users and 2.0 percent of controls, a difference that was not statistically significant. [2]

The CAMELLIA-TIMI 61 trial (about 12,000 participants, five years) found no difference in major adverse cardiovascular events, but more people on lorcaserin were diagnosed with cancer. The trial was designed to measure cardiovascular outcomes rather than cancer. [2] Nausea, headache, dizziness and euphoric mood have been reported, and at doses above the approved range, recreational polydrug users described hallucination-like perceptual changes, attributed to activity at 5-HT2A receptors. [2]

Lorcaserin activates 5-HT2C receptors in the hypothalamus, thought to stimulate POMC neurons and promote satiety. Laboratory characterisation reported selectivity for 5-HT2C over 5-HT2A and 5-HT2B (about 17-fold and 100-fold, respectively). [2][11]

Wikipedia gives an elimination half-life of about 11 to 12 hours, protein binding of about 70 percent, extensive liver metabolism, and 92 percent renal excretion. [2] Pharmacokinetic studies were registered in older adults, people with hepatic impairment, obese adolescents and Japanese and Korean volunteers. [15][16][17][18]
Lorcaserin is a substituted 3-benzazepine, (1R)-8-chloro-1-methyl-2,3,4,5-tetrahydro-1H-3-benzazepine, with the formula C11H14ClN. [2]

Arena Pharmaceuticals submitted a New Drug Application on 22 December 2009. An FDA advisory panel voted 9 to 5 against approval in September 2010, and the FDA declined approval in October 2010, citing the inability to rule out cancer risk and what it judged marginal weight loss; the panel cited mammary tumours in female rats. A later panel in May 2012 recommended approval with restrictions, and the FDA approved it on 27 June 2012. [2]

The DEA proposed Schedule IV classification in December 2012 because of hallucinogenic effects at above-approved doses and possible dependence, and finalised it on 7 May 2013. [2] In February 2020 the FDA requested voluntary withdrawal because of the cancer finding; Eisai withdrew the drug, and the FDA withdrew approval for both formulations on 17 September 2020. [2]

Lorcaserin is not a controlled substance in Canada. [2] In US appearance forums, it appears only as one name in lists of weight-loss prescriptions, such as a 2018 T Nation thread listing Belviq alongside metformin, Victoza, Saxenda and Qsymia. [28] Since its withdrawal, newer prescription weight-loss drugs have taken its place in this discussion.

Registered trials have examined lorcaserin for smoking cessation, drug-resistant epilepsy and chemotherapy-induced neuropathy, although the neuropathy trial was withdrawn and an extended-access epilepsy program is no longer available. [12][13][14] A 12-site trial in cocaine use disorder found no benefit: abstinence was 1.1 percent of 91 participants on lorcaserin and 4.3 percent of 92 on placebo. [26] A pilot study in intermittent explosive disorder reported reduced aggressive responding. [27] The compound has also been explored for Dravet syndrome, though development was reportedly discontinued in late 2024. [2]

The BLOOM, BLOSSOM and BLOOM-DM trials tested weight loss over one year or longer in adults with obesity or overweight. [6][7][8] The CAMELLIA-TIMI 61 safety trial followed about 12,000 participants for five years. [2] A 6-month randomised trial measured abdominal fat loss and metabolic markers; [21] a randomised trial tested weight maintenance after a low-calorie diet; [24] and a small crossover study examined predictors of response. [25] A real-world clinic study and a phase 2 trial with nicotine patch for smoking cessation were also registered. [12][19][20]

card.summary: An FDA-approved prescription weight-loss pill (Belviq) that modestly outperformed placebo in trials and was pulled in 2020 over a cancer signal.
card.note: Withdrawn from the US market in 2020 after a trial found more cancer diagnoses on the drug.

quick.overview:
Lorcaserin was a prescription pill for chronic weight management, approved in the US in 2012. In trials it produced roughly 3 to 3.7 percent more weight loss than placebo over up to a year, with diet and exercise counseling.

In 2020 the FDA requested its withdrawal after a large cardiovascular safety trial reported more cancer diagnoses among users than on placebo.
quick.mechanism: It selectively activates serotonin 5-HT2C receptors in the hypothalamus, which is thought to increase feelings of fullness.
quick.risks: The main documented concern is the cancer imbalance seen in CAMELLIA-TIMI 61. Doses above the approved range have produced hallucinogenic effects, and the DEA classified it as Schedule IV. It is no longer marketed in the US.

chain: Increases satiety and lowers food intake
Weight and abdominal fat loss, leaner appearance
angle.text: Lorcaserin was a prescription appetite-regulating drug. By promoting fullness it helped adults with obesity or overweight lose body fat, which changes the look of the waist, face and overall physique. A 6-month trial reported loss of abdominal fat on the drug.
